title: Oppenheimer recalls the Trinity test and the Bhagavad Gita

tellings.quote: I remembered the line from the Hindu scripture, the Bhagavad Gita. Now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds.
Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom, The Slayer Time, Ancient of Days, come hither to consume;

plain: When the first atomic bomb was tested at the Trinity site in New Mexico in July 1945, J. Robert Oppenheimer later said a line of Hindu scripture came into his head. In a recording played on the show, he says: 'I remembered the line from the Hindu scripture, the Bhagavad Gita. Now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds.' He is the witness here, recalling his own thoughts at the blast. The line comes from a moment in the Gita where the god Krishna reveals his full, terrible form. In Edwin Arnold's English translation of 1885, The Song Celestial, that verse, chapter 11, verse 32, reads: 'Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom.' Oppenheimer does not say which translation he followed, and he read the Gita in Sanskrit, so his words are his own rendering of the same verse, with 'death' where Arnold has 'Time'. The episode uses it to show how the bomb's makers reached for ancient religious language to describe what they had done.

discussion.by: The Song Celestial, or Bhagavad-Gita (translated by Edwin Arnold)
discussion.text: Oppenheimer does not say which translation his words follow, and he read the Gita in Sanskrit; in Edwin Arnold's 1885 translation read here, Krishna's words at chapter 11, verse 32 are "Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom", the same verse in another translator's English. "Now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds" is Oppenheimer's own rendering of it, with death where Arnold has Time.
